subject: american woodcock
title: This Bird Sees Behind Its Head With an Upside-Down Brain

scenes.text: This bird's brain sits upside down in its head, and that's how it stays alive.
The American woodcock's eyes moved so far up and back that its brain got turned over.
The payoff: nearly 360 degrees of vision. It can watch for hawks behind it while its beak is in the mud.
That beak tip bends open underground to grab earthworms, most of its diet.
It even rocks its body as it walks, possibly to make worms move.
And in courtship flights, it flaps along at just five miles an hour. The slowest bird ever timed.

description:
The American woodcock's eyes sit so high and far back on its head that its brain is rotated upside down, giving it a nearly 360-degree field of view.
It probes for earthworms with a flexible bill tip, rocks as it walks, and shares the Guinness record for slowest flying bird at about 5 mph.
